newsitem.title: USA: Don't leave US problems on city doorsteps - group.
newsitem.headline: Don't leave US problems on city doorsteps - group.

text.p: U.S. urban leaders on Monday urged President Clinton and the incoming 105th Congress not to leave the nation's problems and responsibilities on the "doorsteps" of municipal governments, according to a statement released on Monday by the National League of Cities.

The board of directors of the National League of Cities, which meets here this week for its 105th annual conference, adopted seven principles on deficit reduction and entitlement reform that the League's 4,600 delegates are expected to approve on Tuesday, the statement said.

The draft principles, for instance, urge Congress and regulators to revise the Consumer Price Index (CPI) to more accurately report inflation rates and to give states and localities a "reasonable transition time" to prepare for devolution of federal programs.

League President Greg Lashutka, mayor of Columbus, Ohio, also said the group wrote the White House asking for a meeting to "assess and begin to address" a growing shortage of affordable housing in U.S. cities and towns.
The letter cites a $2.7 billion shortfall in low-income federal mortgage assistance and $3.5 billion in cuts of federal public housing assistance over the past three years, the statement says.
It also points to a "looming" $2.3 billion shortfall in federally supported tenant rent subsidies resulting from welfare reform, the statement says.
"This is a disaster waiting to happen," Lashutka said.

He said, "With over one million units of assisted and insured housing units threatend over the next five years, we run the risk of hundreds of thousands of displaced families, serious threats to assessed property values, and grave questions about outstanding federal, state, and local credit and mortgage insurance."

In some of the other draft principles, the League's Board called for "shared sacrifice" by all Americans to eliminate the deficit. "All parts of the federal budget must be on the table," the board said.

The board added that no tax cuts should be considered until Congress enacts balanced budget legislation. And all sides of the deficit reduction debate must use the same economic projections -- those prepared by the Congressional Budget Office, the board said.
